{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tottori Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Shitori Jinja
倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=draft}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|12=draft}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=draft}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=draft}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=draft}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|12=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|8=en}}|天稚彦命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||12=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|12=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|12=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|12=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|12=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|12=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|8=en}}|天稚彦命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||12=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||12=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|12=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|12=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|12=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|12=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. ''Matsuri: The Festivals of Japan''. Routledge Curzon (1996) {{ISBN|1-873410-63-8}} * {{ill|Richard Ponsonby-Fane|Ponsonby-Fane|8=en|12=draft}}, Richard Arthur Brabazon. (1959). [https://books.google.com/books?id=SLAeAAAAMAAJ&q=The+Imperial+House+of+Japan ''The Imperial House of Japan.''] Kyoto: Ponsonby Memorial Society. [[天羽槌雄神|建葉槌命]] ; 配神 * [[シタテルヒメ|下照姫命]] * [[建御名方神|建御名方命]] * [[アメノワカヒコ|天稚彦命]] * [[事代主|事代主命]] * [[スクナビコナ|少彦名命]] * [[アヂスキタカヒコネ|味耜高彦根命]] == 歴史 == [[File:Shitori-jinja, kyouzuka.jpg|thumb|right|220px|{{center|経塚}}]] [[織機|機織]]に携わった[[氏族]]である[[倭文氏]]が祖神の建葉槌命を祀ったのが起源とされている。ただし、社伝には下照姫命に関するものが多く、[[大正]]時代までは下照姫命が主祭神であると考えられていた。社伝によれば、[[出雲]]から渡った下照姫命が現在の湯梨浜町宇野に着船し、御冠山に登って現在地に鎮まったという。着船したと伝えられる場所には、下照姫命が化粧を直したという「化粧水」や、腰を掛けたという「お腰掛岩」などが残っている。これについて、『式内社調査報告』では、元々は織物の神である建葉槌命を祀っていたのが、当地で織物が作られなくなったことにより建葉槌命の存在が忘れられ、共に祀られていた下照姫命だけが残ったと記している。 境内の塚が下照姫命の墓であると考えられていたが、大正4年（[[1915年]]）の発掘により[[経塚]]であることが判明した。その出土品の[[金石文|銘文]]から、当社が[[平安時代]]後期には伯耆国一宮であったことがわかった。このときの出土品である観音菩薩立像などは「伯耆一宮経塚出土品」の名称で、一括して[[国宝]]に指定されている。 戦国時代、当地を治めた武将に社領を没収され荒廃したが、[[天文 (元号)|天文]]23年（[[1554年]]）に[[尼子氏]]が社殿を再建した。また、地元の[[国人]]・[[南条氏]]からも[[寄進]]を受けた。その後当地を治めた[[池田氏]]も崇敬し、[[鳥取藩]]主の[[祈願所]]となった。[[昭和]]14年（[[1939年]]）、国幣小社に列格し、[[第二次世界大戦]]後は[[別表神社]]となった。 かつて主祭神であった下照姫命が女神であることから、安産に霊験があるとされる。本殿の後には、かつて「乳神」と呼ばれる[[神木]]があったが、現在は倒壊している。参道沿いには「安産岩」と呼ばれる岩がある。昔、毎回[[難産]]に苦しんでいた女性が願かけをし、その満願の日の夢に下照姫命が姿を現し、参詣の帰途、この岩の所で簡単に出産したため安産岩と呼ばれるようになったと伝えられる。この岩を削って飲むと霊験があるとされる。 === 創建年代 === 具体的な創建年代は不明であるが、[[平安時代]]初期にあたる[[大同 (日本)|大同]]3年（[[808年]]）の医学書『[[大同類聚方]]』には「川村郡倭文神主之家所傳方　原者下照姫神方也　中暑小便止　頭痛煩熱　口乾者與之」（原文）という記述があり、これが文献上の初見とされている谷田亀寿『[[舎人村 (鳥取県)|舎人村]]郷土史論上代篇』。 == 文化財 == === 国宝 === [[ファイル:伯耆一宮経塚出土品-2.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|伯耆一宮経塚出土品（[[国宝]]）}}{{small|[[東京国立博物館]]展示。}}]] * 伯耆一宮経塚出土品 一括（考古資料） *: 内訳は下記。大正4年（1915年）、社殿の南南東180メートルほどのところにある[[経塚]]（経典を後世に遺すため埋納した塚）から出土した一括遺物。銅[[経筒]]は径20センチ、高さ42.5センチで、円筒形の筒身に宝珠鈕付き、屋根形の蓋を付す。筒身には15行236字の銘文が線刻され、康和5年（1103年）に京尊という僧が埋納したものであることがわかる。出土品のうち、金銅観音菩薩立像は奈良時代にさかのぼる作品である。出土品一括は[[東京国立博物館]]に寄託。『週刊朝日百科 日本の国宝』30号（朝日新聞社、1997年）、pp.2 - 316 - 317 *: 1920年（大正9年）4月15日、当時の[[古社寺保存法]]に基づく旧国宝（現行法の[[重要文化財]]に相当）に指定大正9年4月15日文部省告示第260号で以下の2件が当時の古社寺保存法に基づく旧国宝（現行法の重要文化財に相当）に指定された（参照：[{{NDLDC|2954421}} 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション]）。 *金銅観世音菩薩立像　一躯 *銅経筒 康和五年ノ銘アリ 一口 附 銅造千手観音立像一躯 外出土品一切 1951年6月9日付けで上記2件が1件の重要文化財に統合された（昭和27年5月22日文化財保護委員会告示第14号）。。1953年（昭和28年）3月31日に国宝に指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|845|伯耆一宮経塚出土品}}。 ** 銅経筒 1口 康和五年十月三日伯耆一宮辰巳岳上奉埋納在銘 ** 金銅観音菩薩立像 1躯 ** 銅造千手観音菩薩立像 1躯 ** 銅板線刻弥勒立像 1面 ** 銅鏡 2面 ** 桧扇残片 一括 ** 短刀刀子残闕 一括 ** 瑠璃玉 一括 ** 銅銭 2枚 ** 漆器残片 一括 === 国の史跡 === * 伯耆一宮経塚 - 1935年（昭和10年）12月24日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|2116|伯耆一宮経塚}}。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[鳥取県]][[東伯郡]][[湯梨浜町]]大字宮内754 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[西日本旅客鉄道]]（JR西日本）[[山陰本線]] [[松崎駅 (鳥取県)|松崎駅]] （徒歩約35分） == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 関連図書 == * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』（神社新報社、1968年）32頁 * 白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』（[[東京堂出版]]、1979年）166頁 {{Commonscat|Shitori-jinja}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しとりしんしや}} [[Category:鳥取県の神社]] It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|qq=}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|qq=}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. ''Matsuri: The Festivals of Japan''. (1959). [https://books.google.com/books?id=SLAeAAAAMAAJ&q=The+Imperial+House+of+Japan ''The Imperial House of Japan.''] Kyoto: Ponsonby Memorial Society. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|qq=}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|qq=}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - [[sn:commons:Category:Shitori-jinja]][[en:Shitori Shrine (Tottori)]][[fr:Shitori-jinja]][[ja:倭文神社 (湯梨浜町)]][[zh:倭文神社 (湯梨濱町)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q245734]] Wikidata name: Shitori Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:27, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tottori Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Shitori Jinja
倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|[[:en:Ame no Wakahiko|Ame no Wakahiko]]|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]], the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|qq=}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|qq=}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|1=Ame no Wakahiko|2=zh|3=天稚彥|4=ja|5=アメノワカヒコ|6=az|7=Ame-no-Vakahiko|8=en|qq=draft}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe.
