倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko|WD=Q10940674|lt=Ame no Wakahiko}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|1=Ame no Wakahiko|2=zh|3=天稚彥|4=ja|5=アメノワカヒコ|6=az|7=Ame-no-Vakahiko|8=en|qq=draft}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko|WD=Q10940674|lt=Ame no Wakahiko}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|qq=}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|qq=}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko|WD=Q10940674|lt=Ame no Wakahiko}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko|WD=Q10940674|lt=Ame no Wakahiko}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|1=Ame no Wakahiko|2=zh|3=天稚彥|4=ja|5=アメノワカヒコ|6=az|7=Ame-no-Vakahiko|8=en|qq=draft}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en}}|建御名方命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame-no-wakahiko|1=Ame no Wakahiko|2=zh|3=天稚彥|4=ja|5=アメノワカヒコ|6=az|7=Ame-no-Vakahiko|8=en|qq=draft}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi|8=en}}|事代主命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en}}|少彦名命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|8=en}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. 倭文神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shitori-jinja, haiden.jpg | caption = Haiden of Shitori Jinja Shrine {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Tottori Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|29|25.34|N|133|54|10.68|E|region:JP-35_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto|qq=}}|type = | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} | founded_by = | established = unknown | date_destroyed = | location = 754 Miyauchi, Yurihama-cho, Tohaku-gun, Tottori-ken | website = {{Official|1=https://www.sitorijinja.com}} | architecture_style = ''{{ill|Nagare-zukuri|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagare-zukuri|qq=}}''|festival = 1 May | leadership = | footnotes = {{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=brown|text align=center|{{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site of Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}}}} }} {{nihongo|'''Shitori Shrine'''|倭文神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in the Miyauchi neighborhood of the town of {{ill|Yurihama, Tottori|lt=Yurihama|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yurihama, Tottori|qq=}} in {{ill|Tottori Prefecture|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Japan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan|qq=}}, on the east bank of {{ill|Lake Tōgō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Tōgō|qq=}}. It is the ''{{ill|ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/ichinomiya|qq=}}'' of former {{ill|Hōki Province|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōki Province|qq=}}. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on 1 May.{{cite book|last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} ==Enshrined ''kami''== The ''{{ill|kami|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kami|qq=}}'' enshrined at Shitori Shrine are:{{cite web|title=一ノ宮倭文神社について |url=https://www.sitorijinja.com/about |website=Shitori Jinja official home page |publisher=Shitori Jinja |access-date=17 January 2023|qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}}|建葉槌命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Shitateruhime|ja|下照比売|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|simple|User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}|下照姫命|}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Takeminakata|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeminakata|qq=}}|建御名方命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ame no Wakahiko|en|Ame no Wakahiko|WD=Q10940674|lt=Ame no Wakahiko}}|天稚彦命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}|事代主命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Sukunabikona|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}|少彦名命||qq=draft}} * {{nihongo|{{ill|Ajisukitakahikone|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ajisukitakahikone|qq=}}|味耜高彦根命||qq=draft}} ==History== The origins of Shitori Shrine are unknown. Although there is no documentary evidence, it is believed that it began as the family shrine for the {{Nihongo|Shitori clan|倭文氏}} of {{ill|Kofun period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} craftsmen who weavers, who regarded {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} as their ancestor. However, the shrine's legends are all centered around {{ill|Shitateruhime|lt=Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto|ja|下照比売|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateruhime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シタテルヒメ}}, whom the shrine legend claims arrived in this location from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo-taisha|lt=Izumo Taisha|lt=Izumo|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Taisha|qq=}} by boat. She established her residence on the mountain behind this shrine, and after her death, she was buried in a ''{{ill|kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|qq=}}'' constructed in the shrine's precincts.{{cite book|last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese|qq=draft}} The earliest this shrine appears in documentary records is in the AD 808 medical text {{Nihongo|''Daido-ruishu-ho''|大同類聚方|}}. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}}, the shine was laid to waste, but it was reconstructed by the {{ill|Amago clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amago clan|qq=}} and was later supported by the {{ill|Ikeda clan|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikeda clan|qq=}}, the {{ill|Daimyo|daimyō|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimyo|qq=}} of {{ill|Tottori Domain|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tottori Domain|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Meiji period|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}} era of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}}, the shrine was rated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣中社|Kokuhei Shosha|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|qq=}}.Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. === Hōki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound=== Until the early 20th century, Shitateruhime-no-Mikoto was regarded as the primary deity of this shrine. However, in 1915 an {{ill|archaeological excavation|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/archaeological excavation|qq=}} discovered that the purported {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=''empun''-style circular Kofun|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} was actually a {{ill|sutra mound|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sutra mound|qq=}}. The mound had a diameter of 16-meters and height of 1.6 meters. It contains a rectangular stone box that was 1.2 x 0.9 x 0.5 meters made of {{ill|andesite|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/andesite|qq=}} flat stones. The inside was covered with coarse sand, and contained copper sutra cylinder with inscriptions. The inscription was dated 1103 and was inscribed by monk named Kyoson of the Hōki Ichinomiya. In addition to the sutra cylinder, the box contained a gilt-bronze statue of {{ill|Kannon|lt=Kannon|lt=Guanyin|lt=Kannon Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guanyin|qq=}}, an image of {{ill|Maitreya|Miroku Bosatsu|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maitreya|qq=}} engraving on a copper plate, a bronze mirror, a cypress fan, a short sword, beads, and copper coins. The sutra mounds are valuable in considering the burial memorial service in the Heian period. The sutra mound was designated as a {{ill|Monuments of Japan|lt=National Historic Site|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monuments of Japan|qq=}} in 1935.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2116|title= 伯耆一宮経塚|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=January 2, 2023|qq=draft}} All excavated items are stored at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokyo National Museum|qq=}}.{{cite book|last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403|qq=draft}}{{in lang|ja}} ==location== The shrine is located a 35-minute walk from {{ill|Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|lt=Matsuzaki Station|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuzaki Station (Tottori)|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} {{ill|San'in Main Line|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in Main Line|qq=}}.{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} ==Cultural Properties== ===National Treasures=== *{{nihongo|Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|伯耆一宮経塚出土品||}}{{cite web |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/148928|title=伯耆一宮経塚出土品|trans-title=Hoki Ichinomiya Sutra Mound Excavated Items|language=Japanese |publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agency for Cultural Affairs|qq=}}|accessdate=20 August 2020|qq=draft}} ==Gallery== Shitori-jinja Kyoduka.jpg|Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土 金銅観音菩薩立像・銅造千手観音菩薩立像.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 伯耆一宮経塚出土品.JPG|Recovered artifacts from the Sutra Mound 倭文神社の狛犬 - panoramio.jpg|Komainu ==See also== *{{ill|List of Shinto shrines|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Historic Sites of Japan (Tottori)|qq=}} * {{ill|List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of National Treasures of Japan (archaeological materials)|qq=}} *{{ill|Ichinomiya|8=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}} ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe.
